description: §4.12 (S445, ruling option b; g-wrapped-program-auth-silently-dropped) — a `<program auth="required">` wrapped in a `<div>` at the file root has no `<program>` or `<page>` ancestor, so it IS the file's top-level (application) program and its `auth=` is enforced: the ANONYMOUS document request is redirected to /login and never composes the page, while an AUTHENTICATED viewer's first paint carries the body. Before S445 the wrapper made it top-level to nobody — its `auth=` was dropped with no diagnostic, the emitted server carried CSRF only, and an anonymous POST to its server function returned 200 (reviewer- and PA-executed on c53b297a7).
rationale: §4.12 (S445): 'A `<program>` is top-level if it has no `<program>` or `<page>` ancestor, whatever markup wraps it … Wrapper `<div>`s never change a program's role.' §52.13: '`auth="required"` — every request to this scope SHALL be authenticated; unauthenticated requests are redirected to `loginRedirect=` (default `/login`).'
